title: [EPIC 02] Simplify Credentials for the Internal-Test Profile
source: Original complete issue snapshot used by the 2026-09-12 parent audit; preserved locally before GitHub deletion
redaction: Repeated literal test credential replaced by catalog reference; requirements and scope unchanged
body:
# EPIC: Simplify Credentials for the Internal-Test Profile

## Purpose

Tiny Swarm World is an internal tool for quickly creating reproducible development and test environments. The default `internal-test` profile therefore optimizes for deterministic setup and immediate usability rather than creating unique local credentials on every installation.

Enterprise deployments commonly govern reachability and user identity outside TSW through AD/LDAP, SSO, VPN, firewalls, network segmentation, reverse proxies or other IAM controls. TSW must not duplicate those responsibilities in its basic bootstrap workflow.

## Deterministic internal-test credentials

For the `internal-test` profile, the canonical default password is:

`[canonical internal-test catalog value]`

Human-facing services SHOULD use this value where their password policy permits it. If a component requires a different length, character set, special characters or another credential format, TSW defines one centralized deterministic component-specific test value that satisfies the technical contract.

Machine credentials and bootstrap values must likewise require no manual preparation for the standard internal-test installation. Values with special technical formats, such as encryption/signing keys, tokens or htpasswd material, use centrally defined test-profile values or deterministic derivations that satisfy the consuming component's requirements.

## Override model

The credential resolution model is:

1. configured secure/Infisical override;
2. explicit operator override;
3. deterministic `internal-test` default.

Infisical remains the Vault for environments that require stronger, individual or environment-specific credentials. The standard internal-test profile must remain bootstrappable without an already-running Infisical instance, avoiding circular bootstrap dependencies.

## Security boundary

The deterministic credentials are explicitly **INTERNAL/TEST ONLY**. They are not intended to represent production-grade authentication for publicly reachable environments.

For environments with stronger requirements, operators can replace defaults through the supported Infisical/explicit override mechanism and use enterprise AD/LDAP/SSO/network/IAM controls for reachability and identity governance.

## Simplify the standard path

Remove or isolate credential-generation and recovery mechanisms from the `internal-test` profile when they no longer serve a supported requirement. In particular, audit:

- random default-password generation;
- generated-password recovery state;
- overlapping local credential files;
- duplicate required-credential inventories;
- unnecessary secret-mode branching in the standard path;
- bootstrap dependencies that require Infisical before Infisical can start;
- repository-local state whose only purpose is persisting randomly generated test defaults;
- obsolete compatibility paths without a supported consumer.

Advanced/external-secret workflows may remain when there is a concrete supported use case, but they must be isolated from the normal internal-test installation path.

## WSL2 and native Linux

The normal internal-test installation must work when the repository resides on a Windows-mounted WSL2 filesystem such as `/mnt/d/Projects/Tiny-Swarm-World`. It must not be blocked by filesystem permission requirements for recovery state that is unnecessary when deterministic test credentials are used.

WSL2 and native Linux use the same credential semantics.

## Desired installation flow

```text
clone repository
      -> ./install.sh
      -> resolve deterministic internal-test defaults / configured overrides
      -> bootstrap infrastructure and Infisical
      -> deploy/reconcile services
      -> verify environment
      -> print URLs and login convention
      -> ready for testing
```

The standard path requires no prerequisite password-generation ceremony and no manually maintained credential file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[canonical internal-test catalog value]` is the canonical default password for the `internal-test` profile.
- [ ] Human-facing components use the universal default where technically supported.
- [ ] Components with incompatible credential requirements have centralized, deterministic and documented test-profile alternatives.
- [ ] Machine/bootstrap credentials require no manual preparation for a normal internal-test installation.
- [ ] Special-format cryptographic values satisfy the consuming component's technical requirements.
- [ ] Random default-password generation is removed from the normal internal-test path where it has no remaining requirement.
- [ ] Recovery/persistence machinery used only for randomly generated test defaults is removed from that path.
- [ ] Reinstall/reconcile resolves the same defaults deterministically.
- [ ] A fresh checkout can be installed without first creating a password file.
- [ ] WSL2 installation from `/mnt/d` is not blocked by unnecessary local credential-state permissions.
- [ ] Native Linux has equivalent behavior.
- [ ] Infisical overrides can replace defaults for environments requiring stronger/custom credentials.
- [ ] Explicit operator overrides are supported where appropriate.
- [ ] Self-hosted Infisical does not introduce a circular bootstrap dependency.
- [ ] Documentation clearly marks deterministic defaults as INTERNAL/TEST ONLY.
- [ ] Documentation identifies AD/LDAP/SSO/network/IAM as external enterprise access-governance concerns rather than basic TSW bootstrap responsibilities.
- [ ] Installer output provides enough URL/login information to use the environment immediately.
- [ ] Obsolete credential modes/files/abstractions are removed or isolated behind an explicitly supported advanced use case.
- [ ] Unit/integration tests verify deterministic credential resolution and override precedence.
- [ ] Live/E2E tests verify successful UI logins using internal-test defaults.
- [ ] Live/E2E tests verify configured overrides.
- [ ] Architecture and configuration documentation matches the implemented behavior.

## Three-Amigos Scenarios

### Fresh internal test environment

**Given** a fresh Tiny Swarm World checkout with no custom credentials  
**When** the operator runs `./install.sh`  
**Then** TSW resolves deterministic internal-test credentials  
**And** bootstraps all required services  
**And** the environment is immediately usable with the documented login convention.

### Recreated test environment

**Given** an internal test environment is recreated without overrides  
**When** installation runs again  
**Then** the same deterministic credentials are resolved  
**And** no generated-password recovery file is required.

### Component-specific requirement

**Given** a component cannot accept the universal default  
**When** its credential is resolved  
**Then** TSW uses the centrally defined component-specific deterministic test credential that satisfies its technical contract.

### Stronger environment credential

**Given** an environment supplies a supported Infisical or explicit credential override  
**When** TSW resolves credentials  
**Then** the configured override takes precedence over the internal-test default.

### Enterprise-controlled environment

**Given** the surrounding company infrastructure uses AD/LDAP/SSO, VPN, firewall or other IAM/network controls  
**When** users access TSW services  
**Then** those external systems remain responsible for enterprise identity and reachability governance  
**And** the TSW bootstrap does not duplicate that responsibility.

### WSL2 checkout

**Given** the repository resides under `/mnt/d`  
**When** the internal-test installation runs  
**Then** it is not blocked by permission requirements for unnecessary generated-password recovery state.

## Definition of Done

This EPIC is complete when the deterministic `internal-test` credential model is the actual standard installation path rather than an additional mode beside the previous complexity.

Completion includes implementation cleanup, centralized defaults, documented component exceptions, Infisical/explicit override support, updated architecture/configuration documentation, unit/integration coverage, WSL2 and native-Linux live installation tests, deterministic reinstall verification, UI login verification and override verification.

## Remaining acceptance work — review 2026-09-09
PR #293 is merged; PR #304 integrated the subsequent redacted WSL2 evidence. At candidate `7380f7519eeb05ed49bc5006422895eeebbb20a5`, the recorded final run contains 27 successful browser/service tests with no failures/errors/skips, five successful service authentications, reconcile without credential/source drift, authenticated Portainer restart, and Jenkins matching operator/Infisical override with default HTTP 401 rejection, restoration and cleanup. [Evidence](https://github.com/MatthiasBurger-Coder/Tiny-Swarm-World/blob/b0613ab2fc698c5a97bb0add8afbdcbe931a0adb/.tiny-swarm/evidence/issue-285/live_results_20260909.json). These are bounded historical results, not blanket qualification of current main or native Linux. Vault-only precedence, broader restart/recovery and native parity remain unproved.

CRED-01 through CRED-06 remain integrated. Required continuation:
- [ ] #295 — Close remaining browser/authentication and post-restart host-matrix gaps.
- [ ] #296 — Isolate supported source precedence and complete drift/override parity.

Native target/lifecycle owner: #298; shared WSL2/recovery owner: #299; release owner: #294; final evidence audit: #302. Preserve the original acceptance criteria; merged implementation and bounded successes do not complete unexecuted requirements.
